item.title: Financial Officer
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org The World Bank Group (WBG) Treasury. WBG Treasury is the Vice Presidency (VPU), reporting to the Managing Director and World Bank Group Chief Financial Officer, performing treasury functions for the IBRD, IDA and IFC and, to varying degrees, other members of the World Bank Group and other public and private sector entities. Its activities are organized and grouped into the following divisions: Capital Markets; Asset Management; Client Solutions Structuring; Treasury Operations; Treasury Partnerships Advisory; and Treasury Risk, Compliance Controls. Treasury has been a large and significant participant in the international financial markets for over eighty years and has achieved a global reputation as a prudent and innovative borrower, investor, and risk manager. Treasury is responsible for: (i) managing approximately $300 billion in assets for the World Bank Group and other official sector investors; (ii) leading IBRD's, IDA's and IFC’s triple-A rated financing programs in international and domestic bond and derivative markets; (iii) conducting asset and liability management for IBRD's, IDA’s and IFC's balance sheets; (iv) overseeing the development and outreach related to the financing and hedging products the WBG provides for its developing-country clients; and (v) collaborating with the World Bank member countries to help build their financial markets related capacity through advisory services. Staff in Treasury regularly interact and work with other Departments across the Bank and IFC finance, operations, and investment teams. Treasury Client Solutions Structuring (TRECS) As part of WBG Treasury, the Client Solutions Structuring department (TRECS) provides structuring expertise and advisory services for financial products offered by IBRD, IDA, and IFC – including risk management, structured finance, local currency financing, derivatives and debt capital market solutions. The department has responsibility for asset-liability management and contributes to product innovation and financial policies. Financial Products (TREFP) The Financial Products team, under Treasury Client Solutions Structuring (TRECS) Department, works with the public sector (sovereigns and sub-sovereign entities) to design and implement financial products and provides advisory services that help clients maximize access to development financing and mitigate risks. The WBG Treasury’s Sustainable Finance Program is housed within the TREFP team. The Program is the World Bank Group's leading platform for helping emerging-market governments mobilize private capital through labeled bonds, loans, and other innovative capital-market instruments. To date, the Program has helped public sector borrowers raise over $32 billion from international capital markets, with landmark transactions across emerging markets in every region of the world. The Program operates across the full sustainable finance ecosystem, engaging public sector borrowers, financial regulators, policymakers, institutional investors, national and local governments, state-owned enterprises, and national development banks. Its support spans the structuring and issuance of sovereign and sub-sovereign labeled thematic instruments, including green, blue, and social bonds; the development of green and sustainable finance taxonomies; and advising on regulatory frameworks, strategies, and investor communication. The Program seeks to recruit a financial officer, serving as a sustainable bond structuring adviser, with significant experience in structuring and executing debt capital market transactions to help grow and develop its bond advisory business in emerging markets. The financial officer, based in Washington, DC, will primarily be responsible for providing structuring and execution advice to public-sector borrowers (Ministries of Finance, development banks, state-owned enterprises, cities, and municipalities) on labeled, globally issued thematic bonds. While the primary focus is on bonds and loans, the candidate is also expected to contribute to other areas of innovative product development, research, and knowledge, as applicable. Duties Accountabilities: • Coordinate with relevant government ministries, central banks, and debt management offices to integrate Sustainable Finance Frameworks and strategies into the client's broader debt management strategy. • Advise clients on optimal capital market solutions, propose financing solutions to sector challenges, and achieve sustainable development impact in line with the WBG’s vision and mission. • Advise clients on issuance of labeled thematic bonds; develop bond/loan frameworks, advise on governance arrangements, and how to meet international standards and market expectations. • Guide clients through the Second Party Opinion (SPO) process, helping clients understand the scope, requirements, and implications of external review processes and providing quality assurance support to identify gaps and advise on remediation prior to issuance. • Monitor evolving global sustainable finance trends and relevant regulatory developments and market standards and assess their implications for client strategies and WBG advisory approaches. • Engage with institutional investors — including asset managers, pension funds, insurance companies, and ESG-focused funds — to understand their investment criteria, appetite for sovereign sustainable finance instruments, and expectations regarding framework quality and reporting. • Active relationship management with underwriters and arrangers in multiple jurisdictions • Facilitate investor consultations and roundtables. • Source and onboard a strong pipeline of emerging market clients • Develop and provide training and guidance to WBG operational staff and clients • Support the WBG's broader market development agenda by contributing to thought leadership, market outreach events, and knowledge products related to sovereign sustainable finance. • Undertake research to promote the integrity of the sustainable bond/loan market and write market updates, reports/papers, and guides on sustainable financial solutions. • Collaborate with the WBG Knowledge Bank to establish priority areas for joint efforts; integrate sustainable finance advisory into broader country engagement strategies; and maintain effective working relationships with all. • Draft briefing notes, presentations, framework documentation, and advisory reports with high standards of clarity and technical rigor. • Contribute to the development of TREFP's internal knowledge base on sustainable finance, including preparation of case studies, lessons learned, and best practice guidance notes. • Represent TREFP in internal working groups, external conferences, and forums related to sustainable finance, capital markets, and sovereign debt management. • Mentor and train junior staff. • Assist with other projects or strategy-related activities, as the need may arise. The Financial officer is expected to have a good understanding of financial products offered by multilateral development banks, sustainability challenges and opportunities, and ESG market trends.

item.title: Team Assistant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative changes around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org VPU Context: East Asia Pacific (EAP) is a large and diverse region, ranging from Small Islands States of the Pacific to the Philippines and China. Despite substantial economic growth and poverty reduction, the EAP region faces huge development challenges. Growth has been uneven across and within countries, institutions still need strengthening, and most countries are heavily affected by climate change. The Bank plays a significant role on global public goods, including climate, biodiversity, water pollution, and health. The COVID pandemic, and more recently food and energy price increases are compounding the impact of the global economic slowdown. The World Bank Group is seen as a premier development institution in the region, with a leadership role on analytical and advisory services as well as financing. Unit Context: The World Bank Sydney office serves 2 Pacific divisions: Pacific 1 covers North and South Pacific currently works in nine developing countries in the Region (the Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Samoa, Tonga, and Tuvalu). Pacific 2 covers Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. Over the past years, the World Bank has substantially scaled-up its program and field presence in the Pacific, with a focus on initiatives that address the challenges of fragility, isolation, size and limited capacity, and create a foothold for wider development engagement with emphasis on country-specific strategies along three axes; (i) encouraging regional/global integration; (ii) building resilience against external shocks; and (iii) promoting economic reform and private sector development. The World Bank in the Pacific Islands: https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/pacificislands The successful candidates will be offered three (3) year renewable term appointments. Duties and accountabilities: The Team Assistant (TA) will carry out the full range of office support work, including managing processes and monitoring schedules for Task team leaders and senior staff. The work is varied involving a large amount of research – to ascertain how to perform non routine operational tasks. Most of the tasks will not be standard. The candidate would need to proactively ask questions, use the World Bank intranet and other operational programs, and proactively make connections with staff in other Country Offices and our Washington-based HQ for guidance and advice to achieve the required results. The role will also involve extensive liaison with service units, internal team members both in HQ and in the field, as well as external counterparts. The TA will report functionally to the Manager, Portfolio Operations, who provides supervision and guidance to the office support team. The successful candidate may also be assigned responsibility for some aspects of the unit’s administrative functions. Roles Responsibilities • Work productively and effectively often from own initiative providing support to Task Team Leaders (TTL) and Senior Staff. • Draft routine correspondence, project related documents, and proofread materials using proper grammar, punctuation, and style. • Incorporate agreed comments into documents, making full use of shared drives and software capabilities. • Use word processing, spreadsheets, power point software or desktop publishing skills to produce complex text, reports, figures, graphs, etc., according to standard Bank formats and distribute. • Coordinate schedules taking priorities into account, monitor changes, and communicate information to appropriate staff, inside and outside the immediate work unit, including officials outside the World Bank (WB). • Solve non-routine problems (e.g., responding to requests requiring file searches, and identification of correct operational procedures). • Preparation and logistical planning for various events, such as conferences, workshops, negotiations. • Create AIS, update milestones and tracks assigned tasks, project steps and timetables in the Operational Portal and SAP. • Monitor task budget/trust funds for specific projects on behalf of the team. • Assist with processing Consultant contracts and travel. Coordinate with relevant staff and to provide assistance and/or information on project-related matters when requested. • Maintain current distribution lists, phone/address lists of project/product contacts, and distributes documents for the team. • Maintain up-to-date work unit project and other files (both paper and electronic). • Work will involve frequent interaction with the following: Internal Contacts, Other VP and Global Practice (GP) units, IFC and MIGA, and other institutional units. Staff in all locations, locally and internationally, external Contacts such as Government Officials, Consultants, and External Organizations.

item.title: Intern
item.description: Application Deadline: 31-12-2026 The WTO Secretariat maintains three internship programmes for post-graduate students and recent graduates with an advanced university degree wishing to gain practical experience and deeper knowledge of the multilateral trading system. Only a limited number of such internships is available. Internship selections are based on merit, eligibility criteria, academic qualifications, and expertise. The programmes, listed below, are designed to increase diversity at the WTO, and more information about each may be found in the links provided alongside: (1) The WTO Internship Programme is open to post-graduate students and recent graduates with an advanced university degree from all WTO members and countries or customs territories engaged in accession negotiations - WTO Internship Programme (2) The China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme – Up to ten internships offered under this programme annually, RESERVED FOR POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS OR RECENT GRADUATES WITH AN ADVANCED UNIVERSITY DEGREE FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES - China's LDCs and Accessions Programme (3) the WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies - RESERVED FOR POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES WORKING ON THEIR PH.D THESIS - WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies RULES AND PROCEDURES FOR INTERNS (the following may vary, depending on the programme, so it is best to check the above links for information on a particular programme) Eligibility: A candidate must: be a national of a WTO member state or a country or customs territory engaged in accession negotiations have completed his/her undergraduate studies in a relevant discipline; either: be currently enrolled in a master's degree with at least one year completed; or have completed a master's degree programme and be enrolled in a higher-level postgraduate programme (including doctoral studies); or have completed a postgraduate degree (master's degree or PHD) within the past two years at the time of selection; and be at least 21 years at the time of the internship (and no older than 30 years old at the time of the internship for the China WTO Accessions Internship Programme and China General Internship Programme). A roster of suitable candidates is maintained from which interns are selected. In addition to the internship programmes, the need may also arise to recruit interns at short notice for specific tasks. These recruits will also be drawn from the roster. Names will be maintained on the roster for one year and no more. Contractual Terms and Conditions: An agreement will be established between the intern and the Director of the Human Resources Division, specifying the conditions of service and details of any remuneration. Paid interns receive a daily allowance of CHF 60 (including weekends and official holidays falling within the selected period – Except for interns recruited under the China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme who will receive a daily allowance of CHF 90 ). No other remuneration of any kind shall be paid. Internships take place in Geneva, Switzerland. Travel expenses to and from Geneva cannot be paid by the WTO ( Except for the China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme and for the WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies ) , and such travel is not covered by the Organization's insurance. Interns are responsible for their own insurance cover for illness and accidents for the duration of the internship. Please be aware that the cost of living in Geneva is quite high, and the allowance provided is intended as a supplement. It is important to ensure you have sufficient financial resources to support yourself during your time in the area. Internships are for a minimum of three months and up to a maximum of six months in total with no extension, are dependent on the needs of Divisions, and may commence at any time during the year. Depending on Divisional needs, an internship may be split between two Divisions (3 months and no less in each Division and not exceeding six months in total). In this case, the two internship assignments may be carried out at different times and not consecutively, as long as the applicant meets all the requirements for internship as per the "Eligibility" criteria set out above. It is not permissible to return to the programme at a later date after completing a full six-month internship programme, nor is it permissible to move from one programme to another following a six-month stint. An internship does not, in any way, entail the right to a vacancy in another part of the Secretariat. Interns may, nevertheless, apply to external vacancies. While working at the WTO, interns are not considered as officials or staff members, however, they shall be bound by the same duties and obligations as regular staff members. Interns are expected to work full-time and to carry out the duties assigned to them by their supervisor. On commencing the internship, and as applicable, depending on their nationality and any Swiss residence permit they may hold, interns may be issued with a Swiss legitimation card type "H" which serves as a work and residence permit for the duration of their internship. This link explains the responsibilities of holders of such a card and careful note should be taken of the information provided therein. At the end of the internship, the Supervisor responsible for an intern will write an evaluation report, and the intern will also be required to evaluate the internship. Both evaluations will be placed on file. An internship may be terminated by the WTO Secretariat or by the intern with one week's notice.

item.title: E T Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, www.worldbank.org E astern and Southern Africa Regional Context The Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) region is diverse, spanning low-income and lower-middle-income countries and a number of upper-middle-income borrowers, with wide variation in health outcomes, fiscal space, and institutional capacity. Many countries face a high and evolving burden of disease alongside persistent inequities in access and quality, while also managing recurrent shocks, including climate-related hazards, epidemics, and food and fuel price volatility. In this context, the World Bank supports governments through analytics, policy dialogue, and financing to strengthen human capital and build more resilient health systems and essential public health functions. Through its Health, Nutrition, and Population (HNP) Global Practice, the World Bank supports countries’ efforts towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and providing quality, affordable, equity-focused health services to everyone regardless of their ability to pay by strengthening primary health care systems and reducing the financial risks associated with ill-health. Some of the ongoing health and nutrition challenges in the AFE region include: • Triple burden of disease and epidemiological transition: a continuing burden of communicable diseases (including HIV, TB, malaria and outbreaks), persistently high maternal, newborn and child mortality in many settings, and a rapidly growing burden of NCDs and injuries—often coexisting within the same populations and health systems. • Health system constraints and inequities: persistent gaps in access to quality essential services, especially for rural, remote, and vulnerable populations, driven by constraints in the health workforce, medicines and supply chains, service readiness, governance and accountability, and limited fiscal space and financial protection for households. • Nutrition and food insecurity: high levels of child stunting and micronutrient deficiencies in several countries, alongside rising overweight/obesity, compounded by food price shocks and climate variability that affect diets and worsen vulnerability throughout the life course. Summary of Botswana and Southern Africa Health Portfolio The World Bank’s health portfolio in Botswana combines investment financing with targeted technical assistance (TA) and analytics to advance the Government’s priorities on UHC, primary health care revitalization, and health security. The portfolio is anchored by the Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPRR) Project, which supports preparedness and response; strengthened surveillance, laboratory, and emergency management systems; and investments in core enablers, including digital public health infrastructure and availability of quality data. In parallel, the World Bank provides TA supporting sector planning and governance such as development of the Health Sector Strategic Plan, digital health and data use (interoperability, registries, and routine data quality and use), and improvements in supply chain performance and regulatory systems for health products. This work is complemented by analytics to inform reforms and investments, including on health financing and efficiency, equity, and service delivery performance to strengthen human capital and system resilience. Across southern Africa, the World Bank’s health engagement in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho combines investment lending with analytical and advisory services to strengthen primary health care, improve quality of care, and build more resilient health systems. In Lesotho, the portfolio includes an active health and nutrition system strengthening project focused on expanding coverage and improving the quality of essential maternal and child health, nutrition, and NCD services, alongside reforms to strengthen stewardship and service delivery readiness. There are opportunities to support the preparation of new operations and enhance the scope of TA and advisory work in southern Africa. In South Africa and Namibia, support is anchored in policy dialogue and analytics, including public expenditure and efficiency work, to inform reforms that expand effective coverage, reduce inequities, and improve the sustainability of health financing. Objectives and Scope of Work In light of the growing health portfolio, the HAEH2 team seeks an Extended-Term Consultant (ETC) with experience as a Health Specialist/Economist to provide day-to-day technical and operational support to HNP task teams and Government counterparts, primarily in Botswana and, as needed, across the southern Africa portfolio. The scope of work includes: • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in Botswana. The ETC will support implementation of the Botswana health portfolio (including the HEPRR project) by monitoring progress against the results framework (including support to M E, data quality, and results reporting) and follow-up on agreed actions; supporting planning and delivery of implementation support missions; and contributing to key operational deliverables (aide memoires, management briefs, and client-facing communications). The ETC will help convene consultations with the Ministry of Health and other stakeholders, monitor progress, and coordinate with fiduciary, safeguards, and technical colleagues to ensure timely, integrated support. • Help ensure close coordination with government, development partners, and the CMU and World Bank teams across other sectors in Botswana. The ETC will facilitate coordination and information flow across the Ministry of Health and other relevant agencies, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the Country Management Unit and colleagues in other sectors) to align priorities, timelines, and implementation support. The ETC will play a pivotal role in providing strategic sectoral guidance to the CMU and provide key inputs into country management reviews and documents. • Support policy dialogue with the Ministry of Health, relevant national institutions, and other stakeholders. The ETC will support policy dialogue by preparing briefs, talking points, and presentations, synthesizing implementation experience, sector analytics, and international lessons. The ETC will help translate discussions into clear decisions and follow-up actions to inform priority reforms in primary health care, health security, health financing, and other system strengthening areas. • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in southern Africa, as needed. The ETC will support task teams in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho, including assistance with preparation and follow-up of missions and key deliverables, and contributions to selected analytical and advisory work (e.g., service delivery performance, health financing and efficiency, and health security). Duties and Accountabilities: The ETC’s key tasks and activities will include but are not limited to: • Support implementation support for HEPRR and other Botswana portfolio activities, including monitoring implementation and results; consolidating inputs across technical, fiduciary and ESF colleagues; and proactively following up with counterparts on agreed actions. • Contribute to the planning, preparation, and follow-up of missions, technical consultations, and key portfolio engagements, including drafting agenda/talking points, preparing briefing packages, and drafting aide memoires and progress reports, and management updates as requested by Task Team Leaders. • Support monitoring and evaluation (M E) and results reporting for the portfolio, including maintaining an M E implementation plan, supporting updates to the results framework and indicator definitions as needed, compiling and quality-checking data and narrative inputs for progress reporting. • Provide technical inputs to project implementation, including review of technical specifications and Terms of References for goods and services (e.g., medical and laboratory equipment, digital systems, and technical assistance), and advise on alignment with good practice, user requirements, and World Bank procurement principles (in coordination with procurement specialists). • Support stakeholder coordination across Government, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the CMU and other sectors) by preparing coordination notes, documenting decisions, and escalating issues requiring management attention. • Contribute to selected analytical and advisory activities (ASA), including literature and data review, drafting sections of technical notes and reports, and supporting quality assurance to ensure analytical rigor and consistency of messaging. • As needed, provide operational and analytical support to the southern Africa health portfolio (South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho). • Maintain well-organized records of key documents and correspondence; support timely sharing of information within task teams; and contribute to knowledge management by capturing lessons learned and good practices.

item.title: Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/home Global practice for Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) The Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) Department leads the World Bank Group’s policy dialogue and engagement with countries to strengthen macro-fiscal foundations, including debt sustainability, debt management, public expenditure, and domestic resource mobilization, trade and investment and to accelerate job creation and inclusive growth. FPG links the macroeconomic dialogue with programs focused on expanding the role of the private sector in economic development. In its day-to-day engagement, FPG supports Ministries of Finance, Planning, Economy, Industry and Trade, and Production in pursuing reform agendas that strengthen job creation through inclusive, private sector-led growth. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/topic/fiscal-policy-and-growth Background and general description The FPG unit for Southern Africa and East Africa (EAEM2) is looking for a local economist to be based in Maputo, Mozambique. The selected candidate will contribute substantially to analytical work and lending operations. She or he will report to the FPG Practice Manager covering the EAEM2 unit, which comprises 14 countries across three Country Management Units: AECS1 (South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia), AECS2 (Mozambique, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles), and AECC2 (Angola, Democratic Republic of Congo, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Burundi). The unit has a strong focus on prudent macro-fiscal policies, structural reforms, inclusive growth, and job creation. The World Bank’s FPG engagement in Mozambique supports the country’s efforts to strengthen macroeconomic stability, fiscal and debt sustainability, domestic resource mobilization, and the management of natural-resource revenues, while fostering a more diversified, productive, and job-rich economy. The work program combines policy dialogue, financing operations, technical assistance, and analytical work, including macroeconomic monitoring, Macro Poverty Outlooks, economic updates, public finance analysis, and work on growth and jobs. Particular attention is given to translating Mozambique’s natural-resource potential into broad-based development outcomes, strengthening institutions and fiscal frameworks, and supporting private-sector development and economic resilience. As an Economist for EAEM2, you will contribute to the country team covering Mozambique and, as needed, to the regional FPG team working on other countries. The Economist will be based in Maputo and work closely with the Division Director, Senior Country Economist, Lead Economist, and other members of the country team, and will report to the FPG Practice Manager. The position requires strong analytical capability, sound judgment, close engagement with government counterparts and development partners, and the ability to deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines. The Country Economist will: • Contribute to FPG Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA) in macroeconomic and fiscal management, macroeconomic modelling, data analysis, public finance, growth, jobs, and private-sector development; • Collect, analyze, validate, and maintain economic, fiscal, debt, external-sector, financial, and socioeconomic data related to Mozambique, and communicate findings clearly through tables, charts, briefs, presentations, and analytical notes; • Maintain macroeconomic databases and regularly prepare updated medium-term macroeconomic projections, using economic and financial models and World Bank toolkits; • Contribute to the preparation of Macro Poverty Outlooks, economic updates, public finance and growth diagnostics, Debt Sustainability Analysis, Country Policy and Institutional Assessments, policy notes, and other country and regional knowledge products; • Contribute to the design and implementation of financing operations, including Development Policy Financing, to the design and implementation of SDFP Performance and Policy Actions, and to technical assistance supporting the Government’s reform program; • Serve as a task leader or team member for country-specific financing operations and/or analytical and advisory services, commensurate with experience; • Support the Country Management Unit in implementing the World Bank program in Mozambique and contribute to cross-practice collaboration around country priorities; • Contribute to policy dialogue with government counterparts on macro-fiscal policy, debt, domestic revenue mobilization, natural-resource revenue management, structural transformation, productivity, and job creation; • Establish and strengthen partnerships with bilateral and multilateral agencies, research institutions, academia, civil society, and other stakeholders, helping leverage knowledge and resources; • Contribute to the dissemination of World Bank knowledge products to government, development partners, civil society, academia, the private sector, and other key audiences; and • Contribute to regional and cross-country analytical and operational work within EAEM2 as business needs require.

item.title: E T Temporary - Program Assistant
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . In July2024, the World Bank Group launched the WBG Guarantee Platform (WB GP) a major upgrade to its guarantees business, that will deliver improved guarantee access through a unified team at MIGA as well as innovative new guarantee solutions. These new reforms will help position MIGA to achieve the goal of tripling annual guarantee issuance to $20 billion by 2030. MIGA’s Eastern Europe Regional Office (ECA) is recruiting a one-year Extended Term Temporary (ETT) to provide high-quality administrative, operational, and coordination support to the regional team, contributing to the efficient functioning of business development activities, office operations, information management, and stakeholder coordination. The selected candidate will report to the MIGA Regional Head based in Vienna, Austria, and will work closely with the regional team and relevant World Bank Group stakeholders. Duties and Accountabilities A. Business Development Support • Utilize digital solutions efficiently to support administrative and operational tasks. • Coordinate schedules and calendars, taking priorities into account, and communicate updates to relevant internal and external stakeholders. • Draft routine correspondence and format business documents and presentations. • Coordinate logistics for meetings, workshops, conferences, and events, including invitations, venue arrangements, catering, and related administrative support. • Coordinate mission travel for staff to the region, particularly senior management missions, as well as general staff travel arrangements. • Support the organization of conferences and business development events, including preparation of marketing materials and coordination of meeting facilities. • Establish and maintain lists and databases of clients, partners, and stakeholders. • Contribute to the preparation of marketing and business development materials, particularly PowerPoint presentations and pipeline reports. • Under the guidance of the Regional Head and senior staff, prepare monthly business development activity reports, including retrieval, analysis, and presentation of relevant data. B. Information Management • Maintain and update internal shared resources, databases, and filing systems. • Assist in preparing background materials for meetings and events. • Compile, organize, and distribute documents to relevant participants and stakeholders. • Prepare presentation materials and produce complex texts, reports, figures, charts, and graphs. C. Office Administration and Operations • Manage general office administration, including: o Office inventories and asset tracking o Filing and records management o Courier services and urgent mail delivery o Coordination with vendors and service providers • Process vendor invoices, purchase orders, and non-staff reimbursements through the ePayables Portal. • Work with a high level of professionalism, discretion, and diplomacy in managing priorities and workflow. • Perform ad hoc administrative and operational assignments as required. • Provide backup support to colleagues when necessary. D. HR and Staff Support Coordination • Serve as the regional office coordinator for the Leave and Attendance Record System (LARS). • Coordinate with local HR representatives on administrative HR matters, including: o Staff and dependent visa renewals and expirations o UNLP documentation o Local employment permits and exemptions o Related follow-up actions and documentation support 4. Required Competencies and Skills • Strong organizational and multitasking skills • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Russian • High level of attention to detail and professionalism • Ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office applications • Experience with MIGA or WBG internal systems, business processes is a must • Familiarity with AI-enabled productivity tools and digital collaboration platforms • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multicultural environment • Strong interpersonal skills and client-oriented approach • Ability to handle confidential information with discretion

item.title: E T Temporary
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. Visit http://www.worldbank.org/ Regional Context The Middle East and North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan Region serves twenty two countries across different income groups, of which fourteen are active/potentially active IBRD/IDA borrowers (Afghanistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Syria, West Bank and Gaza, Tunisia, and Yemen), with a total of 251 projects and over $51 bn in total commitment. Eight are users of the Region's non-lending services, mostly on a reimbursable basis (Bahrain, Kuwait, Libya, Malta, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates). The mission of the region is to foster sustainable growth with a focus on job creation and poverty reduction, economic and social inclusion, and good governance. The region attaches importance to creating a supportive work environment based on the values of teamwork, transparency, trust, and client service, underlined by professional excellence. The region places high value on diversity. The region is organized into seven Country Departments (CMUs), the Office of the Regional Chief Economist, and the Development Effectiveness Unit (MNADE). With an expanded regional strategy, the World Bank aims to help the region weather the current crises, move from stabilization to transformation, unlock its vast economic potential of youth and women, develop its human capital to adapt to global megatrends, and foster innovation ( https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/mena ). Djibouti is one of the smallest countries in Africa, with an area of 23,200 square kilometers and a population estimated at about 990,000. The size of its economy limits its ability to diversify production and increases its reliance on foreign markets, making it more vulnerable to market downturns and hampering its access to external capital. With less than 1,000 square kilometers of arable land (0.04% of its total land area) and average annual rainfall of only 130 millimeters, Djibouti depends almost completely on imports to meet its food needs. As of June 2026, Djibouti’s active portfolio comprised 17 IDA projects worth about US$501 million. The portfolio is focused on energy, transport, digital transformation, education, health, social safety nets, energy, rural community development, slums upgrading and urban poverty reduction, governance, and private sector development, with an emphasis on women and youth. For more information on Djibouti, please visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/djibouti Roles Responsibilities: The Extended Term Temporary (ETT) will perform several functions, including, but not limited to: Main Tasks: Resource Management: • Serve as the primary liaison for vendors, assisting them with any inquiries related to their payments. • Facilitate the identification of accrual amounts and ensure timely follow-up with vendors to secure prompt submission of invoices. • Support the creation of purchases orders and registration of vendors • Document all relevant supporting elements for adequate RM monitoring • Monitor and report on resource usage • Coordinate with various GPs and team members to ensure efficient use of charge codes, supporting documents • Liaise with the RM team based in Cairo and other relevant units to ensure CO satisfactory score card Support to Global Practices: • Assist the GPs with administrative, mission and logistical support • Handles mission planning and preparation • Schedule and coordinate meetings, appointments, and travel arrangements with external stakeholders/clients • Prepare and distribute meeting agendas, minutes, and other relevant documents • Maintain and organize files, records, and documentation • Support the GPs in their day-to-day activities and tasks during the missions • Offer administrative support to the office in facilities, administration, procurement, and finance as need be • Assist with recruitment processes and coordinate logistics for high-level visits, as need be • Other tasks (back up program assistant in case of absence of main program assistant)

item.title: The Nuclear Energy Agency - Software Engineer
item.description: Main Responsibilities Software Infrastructure Development Modernise the CPS Workflow: develop a secure, efficient software and database infrastructure to streamline code and benchmark distribution. Work with NEA colleagues to ensure the effective integration of new software into broader NEA IT infrastructure and facilitate logging and reporting of CPS distribution activities. Maintain and monitor relevant Data Bank digital services, interfaces and associated infrastructure, applying modern best practices in all areas of your work, including the re-implementation of functionality from legacy codebases to other programming languages while ensuring consistency of business logic and system behaviour. Assist senior staff with the implementation and maintenance of new API-enabled frameworks for the management of nuclear physics data, nuclear energy experimental data, and other data, as required. Communication and Liaison Develop good working relationships and close contacts across the Agency and Data Bank to understand software and database needs across the business and act as a contact point for scientific software solutions. Work closely with Data Bank staff to understand user needs and advise on software and DevOps solutions. Report on and present the work of the NEA Data Bank in your area of work to internal and external audiences. Other Carry out other related duties as assigned by the Head of the Data Bank.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: L’Agence pour l’énergie nucléaire - Ingénieur(e) logiciel
item.description: Responsabilités principales Développement de l’infrastructure logicielle Moderniser le flux de travail du CPS : développer une infrastructure logicielle et de bases de données sécurisée et efficace afin de rationaliser la distribution des codes et des benchmarks. Travailler avec les collègues de l’AEN afin d’assurer l’intégration efficace des nouveaux logiciels dans l’infrastructure informatique plus large de l’AEN et de faciliter la journalisation et le reporting des activités de distribution du CPS. Maintenir et surveiller les services numériques, interfaces et infrastructures associées pertinents de la Banque de données, en appliquant les meilleures pratiques modernes dans tous les domaines de travail, y compris la réimplémentation de fonctionnalités issues d’anciens codes dans d’autres langages de programmation, tout en garantissant la cohérence de la logique métier et du comportement du système. Aider le personnel senior à mettre en œuvre et à maintenir de nouveaux cadres activés par API pour la gestion des données de physique nucléaire, des données expérimentales relatives à l’énergie nucléaire et d’autres données, selon les besoins. Communication et liaison Développer de bonnes relations de travail et des contacts étroits au sein de l’Agence et de la Banque de données afin de comprendre les besoins en matière de logiciels et de bases de données dans l’ensemble des activités, et agir comme point de contact pour les solutions logicielles scientifiques. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le personnel de la Banque de données afin de comprendre les besoins des utilisateurs et de conseiller sur les solutions logicielles et DevOps. Rendre compte et présenter les travaux de la Banque de données de l’AEN dans votre domaine de travail à des publics internes et externes. Autres Exécuter toute autre tâche connexe confiée par le/la Chef(fe) de la Banque de données.

item.title: Project Coordinator – Space Management
item.description: EXD/CSI/BID is looking for a Project Coordinator who will contribute to the implementation of the Organisation’s space management strategy and to the delivery of space planning projects and initiatives. The selected candidate will work hands-on on a range of projects and activities related to office space management, workplace planning and office moves, while supporting the effective use of space management tools and applications. The selected candidate will work under the supervision of the Head of the Space Planning Unit. Main Responsibilities Space Projects, Relocation and Densification Coordinate office planning, relocation and densification projects from needs assessment through implementation, in collaboration with internal clients and technical teams. Gather user requirements and prepare project briefs, feasibility studies, layout options, schedules and cost estimates to support decision-making. Prepare plans, technical specifications and requests for quotation, and coordinate the delivery of works by architects, contractors and other service providers. Integrate technology requirements into new spaces including meeting rooms and connectivity. Ensure compliance with the fire safety and accessibility requirements, including for people with reduced mobility, and promote workstation ergonomics. Identify and mitigateproject risks related to schedule, budget and business continuity during works. Monitor project schedules, expenditure and risks, escalating issues and helping to ensure timely delivery, business continuity and the effective use of resources. Coordinate day-to-day officemoves based on internal client requests received through the ticketing system, in collaboration with other technical services and verify the delivery and installation of furniture and equipment. Space Data and Performance Analysis Maintain accurate plans and inventory and records of space allocated to each directorate, in coordination with directorate resource managers, using 2D plans and dashboards. Liaise with finance and internal clients to anticipate future needs and determine the allocated surfaces for chargeback purposes. Analyse occupancy rates using sensor and badge data to support the right-sizing of spaces Prepare KPI reporting for management, including occupancy rates, cost per m² and density Conduct post-move satisfaction surveys, gather user feedback and implement corrective adjustments as needed. Procurement, Suppliers and Furniture Management Support Regularly inspect the condition of furniture, to ensure user safety. Update Inventory records and prepare documentation required for furniture disposal. Organise furniture repairs and maintenance carried out by external service providers. Coordinatee tenders and contribute to the selection of service providers, including movers, furniture suppliers, project manager consultants and work contractors. Client service and internal stakeholder engagement Build close working relationships with internal stakeholders, with a strong focus on client service. Contribute to the development of communication tools tailored to client needs, in line with established processes. Apply existing communication strategies to promote projects and workspaces, increasing their visibility and adhere to all OECD communication standards and best practices, liaising with the Communications Directorate as needed.Actively cooperate with various OECD services, including Procurement, Finance, Security, Quality, Health and Environment, and IT.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: Statisticians-Data analysts
item.description: Main Responsibilities Data collection and dataset management Gather data from OECD member and non-member countries, develop and implement innovative and efficient approaches to data collection, including the use of digital data sources, automated data collection and data transfer solutions and AI-assisted methods where appropriate. Convert national data collected from countries into specific OECD formats, including data manipulation and various other analytical calculations, using efficient, reproducible and increasingly automated data-processing workflows. Verify the accuracy, coherence, quality and internal consistency of the data and metadata using appropriate validation procedures, automated quality checks and other modern data-quality tools. Manage statistical databases covering the range of statistical activities relevant to the work area, ensuring that data are well structured, documented, accessible and fit for analytical and dissemination purposes. Update and maintain the international comparability of data including methodological changes (e.g. when new international definitions are introduced), and research new data and data sources to expand the database coverage, including non-traditional and emerging sources where relevant. Build and maintain contacts with statistical staff in national and other international statistical agencies, with a view to improving data coverage, relevance and availability of methodological information, data transfer and timeliness. Keep abreast of the work of other international and national organisations (e.g. UN, Eurostat, the World Bank) on topics relevant to the Department’s statistical work, as well as developments in statistical standards, data technologies and emerging sources of data. Analysis, methodology, drafting, documentation and presentation Use advanced and innovative statistical and analytical methods to analyse data with the objective of reporting on the main findings, using individual country level or cross-country data. Participate in the drafting and production of statistical and analytical publications and/or reports. Develop clear, accurate and compelling charts to communicate statistical findings and analytical results effectively to technical and non-technical audiences and present complex data in an accessible and policy-relevant manner. Contribute to improving the design of questionnaires in order to extend data coverage, enhance their relevance and improve the availability of methodological information, data transfer and timeliness, including by considering opportunities for digital data collection and alternative sources of information. Develop suitable data solutions to support ECO’s policy research and economic analysis, including integrated datasets, analytical tools and reproducible data pipelines where appropriate. Respond to the changing needs of users by contributing to statistical development work. Develop and maintain clear documentation on work procedures covering all aspects of the production cycle and all aspects of the national data (e.g. methodologies) IT work and other tasks Develop and adapt computer programmes and procedures in a variety of statistical packages (e.g. R, Python or STATA and other appropriate data-processing and analytical tools). Develop, maintain and improve reproducible and automated workflows for data collection, processing, validation, analysis and dissemination, making effective use of modern programming and data-management technologies. Assist in the preparation of data files used in the dissemination of data (e.g. OECD Data Explorer, CSV) and in establishing the layout of documents and publications. Carry out statistical work in support of the wider analytical work of the directorate.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: Statisticien(ne)s-Analystes de données
item.description: Responsabilités principales Collecte de données et gestion d’ensembles de données Rassembler des données auprès de pays membres et non membres de l’OCDE, élaborer et mettre en œuvre des approches innovantes et efficientes de la collecte de données, y compris l’utilisation de sources de données numériques, la collecte automatisée de données et les solutions de transfert de données, ainsi que les méthodes fondées sur l’IA le cas échéant. Convertir les données nationales recueillies auprès des pays dans les formats propres à l’OCDE, comprenant la manipulation de données et divers autres calculs analytiques ainsi que l’utilisation de flux de traitement des données efficients, reproductibles et de plus en plus automatisés. Vérifier l’exactitude, la cohérence, la qualité et l’homogénéité des données et métadonnées en appliquant des procédures de validation appropriées, des contrôles de qualité automatisés et d’autres outils modernes de qualité des données. Gérer les bases de données statistiques couvrant l’éventail d’activités statistiques relevant du domaine de travail, en veillant à ce que les données soient bien structurées, documentées, accessibles et adaptées à l’analyse et à la diffusion. Assurer la mise à jour et le maintien de la comparabilité à l’échelon international des données, notamment lors de changements méthodologiques (introduction de nouvelles définitions internationales, par exemple), et rechercher de nouvelles données et sources de données afin d’étendre le champ couvert par les bases de données, y compris des sources non traditionnelles et nouvelles le cas échéant. Nouer et entretenir des contacts avec le personnel des autorités statistiques nationales et d’autres offices statistiques internationaux, dans le but d’améliorer la couverture des données, la pertinence et la disponibilité des informations de nature méthodologique, le transfert des données et leur actualité. Rester au fait des activités menées par d’autres organisations nationales et internationales (par exemple, ONU, Eurostat, Banque mondiale) sur les sujets pertinents pour les travaux statistiques du Département, ainsi que des évolutions des normes statistiques, des technologies de données et des nouvelles sources de données. Analyse, méthodologie, rédaction, documentation et présentation Utiliser des méthodes statistiques et analytiques avancées et innovantes pour analyser les données en vue de rendre compte des principales conclusions, en utilisant des données par pays ou des données internationales. Participer à la rédaction et à la production de publications et/ou rapports statistiques et analytiques. Préparer des graphiques clairs, précis et convaincants afin de communiquer efficacement les conclusions statistiques et les résultats d’analyse à des publics spécialisés et non spécialisés, et présenter des données complexes de manière accessible et pertinente. Contribuer à l’amélioration de la conception des questionnaires afin d’améliorer la couverture des données, leur pertinence, la disponibilité des informations méthodologiques ainsi que le transfert des données et leur communication en temps opportun, y compris en étudiant les possibilités offertes par les méthodes numériques de collecte de données et les autres sources d’information. Élaborer des solutions de données adaptées à l’appui des travaux de recherche sur l’action publique et d’analyse économique conduits par ECO, y compris des ensembles de données intégrés, des outils d’analyse et des pipelines de données reproductibles le cas échéant. Répondre à l’évolution des besoins des utilisateurs en contribuant aux travaux de développement statistique. Élaborer et tenir à jour des documents clairs sur les procédures de travail relatives à tous les aspects du cycle de production et des données nationales (méthodologies, par exemple). Travaux informatiques et autres tâches Élaborer des procédures et les programmes informatiques faisant appel à divers logiciels statistiques (ex. : R, Python ou STATA et d’autres outils appropriés d’analyse et de traitement des données) et les adapter. Élaborer des flux de tâches reproductibles et automatisés pour la collecte, le traitement, la validation, l’analyse et la diffusion de données, en assurer la maintenance et l’amélioration, en faisant une utilisation efficace des technologies modernes de programmation et de gestion de données. Aider à préparer les fichiers utilisés pour la diffusion des données (sur l’Explorateur des données de l’OCDE, au format CSV, par exemple) et participer à l’élaboration du format des documents et des publications. Mener des travaux statistiques à l’appui des travaux analytiques plus généraux de la Direction.

item.title: Head of PARIS21 Secretariat
item.description: Main Responsibilities Strategic Leadership Provide strategic direction to the Partnership to enable the achievement of its objectives. Ensure the effective delivery of advocacy messages and promote the culture of evidence-based policy-making and decision-making. Engage with key stakeholders involved in statistical capacity development at the country level and in international processes. Drive innovation in statistical capacity development, including modernisation of national statistical systems and strengthening of country-led data ecosystems. Strengthen strategic planning for statistics,including the design and implementation of National Strategies for the Development of Statistics (NSDS), and support efforts to enhance national statistical capacity development, data use and impact. Support and facilitate the development of global, regional and national networks to achieve PARIS21 objectives and engage with emerging statistical development initiatives. Representation, Partnerships and Advocacy Represent PARIS21 within the OECD and externally at high-level international, regional and national fora. Establish and maintain strategic partnerships with governments, national statistical offices, international and regional organisations, donors, academia, civil society and the private sector. Promote evidence-based policy making and support efforts to strengthen investment in data and statistics. Strengthen PARIS21’s visibility, credibility and influence within the international statistical and development communities. Management, Resource Mobilisation and Oversight Lead resource mobilisation efforts for PARIS21, including engagement with existing and prospective donors, and identification of new funding opportunities. Oversee the planning, implementation and monitoring of the Programme of Work and Budget, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and delivering high-quality results. Lead and manage the staff of the PARIS21 Secretariat in support of the Partnership’s business needs. Set objectives and provide guidance on the goals, direction and timing of their work; provide regular and constructive feedback on performance to motivate staff and contribute to their professional development. Develop and maintain good teamwork and ensure effective work methods and project management; implement and maintain arrangements to ensure effective internal communications. Build and lead a cohesive, multicultural and multidisciplinary team, promoting excellence, inclusion and diversity. Actively manage the Secretariat’s human capital through merit-based recruitment, performance management, professional development and staff well-being, in line with OECD rules and values. Adhere to and promote the highest professional standards and the ethical principles of the OECD's Code of Conduct in all internal and external matters. Ensure a caring environment where managers promote, respect and support staff in developing their full potential.

item.title: Energy Analysts - PAL5-PAL6
item.description: Main Responsibilities Research and Analysis Undertake quantitative and qualitative analysis of energy trends and policies at the global, regional and country level. Carry out analytical work on assessing the status, costs, prospects and potential of technologies in the electricity and energy sectors, as well as in end-use sectors. Work with policy makers to collaboratively develop analysis, strategies, and policies to support goals in the field of energy. Provide the Secretariat with insights and updates concerning the status of technologies, progress in the field, innovation, and R&D priorities. Co-author and contribute to relevant IEA outputs, including project reports, web content, training material, presentations, and input to other IEA products. Seek opportunities to attract funding from like-minded partners. Liaison and Outreach Coordinate the Secretariat support with relevant stakeholders and partners. Foster their interaction and collaboration with the IEA’s committees and standing groups. Collaborate with relevant colleagues across the Agency in support of the broader IEA efforts and strengthen IEA engagement with other collaborative platforms. Promote the work of the IEA externally to a wide range of audiences through organising and participating in workshops, making presentations, and holding bi-lateral meetings. Participate in preparations for meetings of IEA standing committees, working parties and other groups as required; participate in relevant meetings of other international organisations; provide support for the development of reports, analyses and information items for these meetings. Maintain contacts with members of national delegations, other international organisations, representatives of industry, and other institutions involved in energy market assessments.
item.dc:creator: OECD

item.title: Analystes en énergie PAL5-PAL6
item.description: L’AIE cherche à recruter plusieurs analystes en énergie, en vue de constituer un vivier de candidat(e)s pour répondre à ses besoins actuels et futurs. Ces personnes collaboreront avec, entre autres, les équipes responsables des travaux sur les Perspectives énergétiques mondiales, les Perspectives des technologies de l’énergie, les transitions vers les énergies propres, l’efficacité énergétique et les marchés de l’énergie, et contribueront à l’analyse des tendances énergétiques régionales et sectorielles à long terme, des choix technologiques de demain et de l’évolution des marchés. Les candidat(e)s retenu(e)s auront une solide expérience de l’analyse énergétique, avec une spécialisation dans un ou plusieurs secteurs (industrie, transports, bâtiment, production d’électricité, approvisionnement en énergie bas carbone, marchés des combustibles fossiles, technologies liées aux énergies renouvelables). Elles/Ils prêteront leur concours aux travaux d'analyse et de rédaction nécessaires à l’élaboration des publications thématiques à fort retentissement de l’AIE, en couvrant un large éventail de thèmes en lien avec l’énergie (par exemple, feuilles de route nationales de transition vers la neutralité carbone, feuilles de route des technologies et examens sectoriels approfondis, rapports sur les marchés, transitions vers les énergies propres). L'AIE recherche notamment des experts dans des domaines tels que les marchés pétroliers, les minéraux critiques, l'investissement énergétique, la sécurité énergétique, la politique de l'électricité, la coopération énergétique régionale, l'efficacité énergétique, les énergies renouvelables, les technologies et l'innovation énergétiques, les transitions énergétiques et la coordination multilatérale. De plus amples informations concernant l’AIE et ses travaux sont disponibles à l’adresse www.iea.org .

item.title: Coordinateur/trice de projet - Gestion des locaux
item.description: EXD/CSI/BID recherche un coordinateur ou une coordinatrice de projet, qui contribuera à mettre en œuvre la stratégie de gestion des locaux de l’Organisation et à mener à bien les projets et les initiatives d’aménagement de l’espace. La personne retenue s’occupera de façon concrète de divers projets et initiatives en lien avec la gestion des espaces de bureaux, l’aménagement de l’environnement de travail et les déménagements de bureaux, tout en soutenant une utilisation efficace des outils et des applications de gestion de l’espace. Elle travaillera sous la supervision du Chef de l’unité de l’aménagement de l’espace. Responsabilités principales Projets relatifs aux espaces de bureaux, déménagement et densification Coordonner les projets d’aménagement des bureaux, de déménagement et de densification, de l’évaluation des besoins à la mise en œuvre, en collaboration avec les clients internes et les équipes techniques. Recueillir les besoins des utilisateurs et préparer les synthèses de projet, les études de faisabilité, les différentes configurations envisageables, les calendriers et les estimations des coûts afin d’étayer la prise de décision. Préparer les plans, les spécifications techniques et les demandes de devis, et coordonner le déroulement des travaux des architectes, des sous-traitants et des autres prestataires de services. Intégrer les exigences en matière de technologie dans les nouveaux espaces, dont les salles de réunion et la connectivité. Veiller à la conformité aux exigences en matière de prévention des incendies et d’accessibilité, notamment pour les personnes à mobilité réduite, et promouvoir l’ergonomie des postes de travail. Repérer et atténuer les risques des projets relatifs au calendrier, au budget et à la continuité de l’activité pendant les travaux. Assurer le suivi du calendrier des projets, des dépenses et des risques, en faisant remonter les problèmes et en garantissant une exécution en temps voulu, la continuité de l’activité et l’utilisation des ressources. Coordonner les déménagements de bureaux au quotidien, sur la base des demandes des clients internes reçues via le système de tickets, en collaboration avec d’autres services techniques, et contrôler la livraison et l’installation du mobilier et du matériel. Analyse des données et des performances des espaces de bureaux Tenir à jour les plans, l’inventaire et les registres des espaces alloués à chaque direction, en coordination avec les gestionnaires des ressources dans les directions, au moyen de plans 2D et de tableaux de bord. Assurer la liaison avec les services financiers et les clients internes afin d’anticiper les besoins à venir et de déterminer les surfaces allouées à des fins de refacturation. Analyser les taux d’occupation au moyen des données issues des capteurs et des badges afin d’adapter la taille des locaux aux besoins. Préparer la communication des KPI à la direction, dont les taux d’occupation, le coût par m² et la densité. Mener des enquêtes de satisfaction auprès des utilisateurs à l’issue du déménagement, recueillir les retours d’information utiles et prendre des mesures correctives le cas échéant. Achats, fournisseurs et soutien à la gestion du mobilier Procéder à des inspections régulières du mobilier, afin de garantir la sécurité des utilisateurs. Tenir à jour les registres d’inventaires et préparer la documentation nécessaire à la mise au rebut du mobilier. Organiser les réparations et l’entretien du mobilier par des prestataires de services externes. Coordonner les offres et contribuer à la sélection des prestataires de services, notamment les entreprises de déménagement, les fournisseurs de mobilier, les consultants en gestion de projet et les sous-traitants pour les travaux. Service client et participation des parties prenantes internes Nouer des relations de travail étroites avec les parties prenantes internes, en attachant une grande importance au service client. Contribuer à la conception d’outils de communication adaptés aux besoins des clients, conformément aux processus établis. Appliquer les stratégies de communication en vigueur afin de promouvoir les projets et les espaces de travail en accroissant leur visibilité, et respecter l’ensemble des normes et bonnes pratiques de l’OCDE en matière de communication, en coopérant avec la Direction de la communication en tant que de besoin. Coopérer activement avec les divers services de l’OCDE, notamment ceux responsables des achats, de la finance, de la sécurité, de la qualité, de la santé et de l’environnement, ainsi que de l’informatique.
